docs.text: Agenda Day 1 Industry Trends in Java and IBM Liberty Technical Overview IBM Liberty is a modular Java application server built to support scalable cloud-native application styles with technical advantages over Apache Tomcat and Spring Boot. It's the highest-performing and most modular application runtime in the world! Hands on Labs – Using IBM Liberty on VMs and Containers, Deployment, Best Practices Dive deep on usage of IBM Liberty in virtual machines and containers, how IBM Liberty streamlines configuration and deployment including best practices. Dive Deeper: Optimizing Liberty in Containers and on Hyperscalars Learn how to tune IBM Liberty and Java for scale-out, high performant systems including best practices for container configuration. Learn tuning and optimization. Make your Java environments hum in containers and hyperscalers. Day 2 AI-Driven Java Modernization with Application Modernization Accelerator and Watson Code Assistant for Java Learn how IBM’s industry-leading Java application environment analysis and code modernization tools can accelerate Java modernization by automating code remediation. Live demo. Go Deeper in AI-Driven Java Modernization with IBM’s Managed Enterprise Application Service for Java (EaSEJ) IBM offers a fully managed cloud service for hosting Java applications with support for messaging, databases, and tooling to automate the migration. A managed service! Live demo, learning about this innovative solution. Managing Traditional WebSphere and IBM Liberty Applications Side-by-Side using IBM’s Modernized Runtime Extension for Java (MORE) With IBM’s Modernized Runtime Extension for Java (MoRE), WebSphere customers can manage both traditional WebSphere applications and IBM Liberty applications using the WebSphere Admin Console and supporting management capabilities – easing the management for Liberty applications. Lab Competitive Differentiation : Winning with IBM Liberty in the Market Understanding positioning and strengths of IBM Liberty against competitors. Dive Deep with AI-Driven DevOps with IBM DevOps Loop IBM’s DevOps Loop accelerates and optimizes software delivery with an open, AI-augmented DevSecOps platform. IBM DevOps Loop streamlines the toolchain and enable teams to start projects quickly and deliver value fast. See it in action!

docs.text: Day 1: Accessing lab environment Go to the Attendee Lab URL from the Day 1 Labs menu item, From the Day 1 Labs menu item, select the Lab Environment URL for the specific lab(s) you want to run Enter the workshop password: websphere and click Submit button Click the URL to your environment and enter the password that is displayed on the page, which is unique to your environment. The VMs will be shown, and should already be STARTED DO NOT start / stop VMs unless instructed to do so! You will see a screen with one or more VMs, depending on the specific lab. Follow the lab guide for instructions for accessing the specific VM, credentials, etc. Note: The lab guides include the information for which VM to open, how to login to the VM, login credentials, etc. Liberty lab fix for pom.xml file Replace the contents of pom.xml file in the following directory, with this new content. /home/ibmdemo/Student/labs/devmode/demo-project and <groupId>org.eclipse.microprofile</groupId> <artifactId>microprofile</artifactId> <version>3.3</version> <type>pom</type> <scope>provided</scope> </dependency> <!-- For tests --> <dependency> <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId> <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId> <version>5.6.2</version> <scope>test</scope> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>org.apache.cxf</groupId> <version>1.1.4</version> <scope>test</scope> </dependency> </dependencies> <build> <finalName>${project.artifactId}</finalName> <plugins> <!-- Enable liberty-maven plugin --> <plugin> <groupId>io.openliberty.tools</groupId> <artifactId>liberty-maven-plugin</artifactId> <version>3.3.4</version> <configuration> <assemblyArtifact> <groupId>io.openliberty</groupId> <artifactId>openliberty-javaee8</artifactId> <version>21.0.0.3</version> <type>zip</type> </assemblyArtifact> </configuration> </plugin> <plugin> <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>maven-war-plugin</artifactId> <version>3.2.3</version> </plugin> <plugin> <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId> <version>2.22.2</version> </plugin> <!-- Plugin to run functional tests --> <plugin> <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>maven-failsafe-plugin</artifactId> <version>2.22.2</version> <configuration> <systemPropertyVariables> <http.port>${liberty.var.default.http.port}</http.port> </systemPropertyVariables> </configuration> </plugin> </plugins> </build> </project>
